dn20:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling amongst the Sakyans in the Great Wood near Kapilavatthu with a great Saṅgha of monks consisting of five hundred monks, all of them Worthy Ones,
dn20:1.3: and almost all of the gods from the ten world-elements had assembled to see the Fortunate One and the Saṅgha of monks.
dn20:2.1: Then this occurred to four gods from among the hosts in the Pure Abodes:
dn20:2.2: “The Fortunate One is dwelling amongst the Sakyans in the Great Wood near Kapilavatthu with a great Saṅgha of moṅks consisting of five hundred monks, all of them Worthy Ones,
dn20:2.3: and almost all of the gods from the ten world elements have assembled to see the Fortunate One and the Saṅgha of monks.
dn20:2.4: Well now, we too could approach the Fortunate One, and after approaching the Fortunate One we could recite a verse each in his presence.”
dn20:3.1: Then those gods, just as a strong man might stretch out a bent arm, or bend in an outstretched arm, in the same way disappeared from among the gods of the Pure Abodes and appeared in front of the Fortunate One.
dn20:3.2: Then those gods after worshipping the Fortunate One, stood on one side.
dn20:3.3: While standing on one side one of the gods recited this verse in the presence of the Fortunate One:
dn20:3.4: “There is a great convention in the wood,
dn20:3.5: and a host of gods have come,
dn20:3.6: we have come to this Dhamma convention
dn20:3.7: to see the Saṅgha, who are undefeated.”
dn20:3.8: Then another god recited this verse in the presence of the Fortunate One:
dn20:3.9: “In this place the monks are concentrated,
dn20:3.10: they have straightened out their minds by themselves,
dn20:3.11: like a charioteer who has taken the reins,
dn20:3.12: the wise protect their sense faculties.”
dn20:3.13: Then another god recited this verse in the presence of the Fortunate One:
dn20:3.14: “Having cut off the hindrance and obstacle,
dn20:3.15: and dug up the locking post, they are unmoved,
dn20:3.17: young nāgas, well-tamed by the Visionary.”
dn20:3.18: Then another god recited this verse in the presence of the Fortunate One:
dn20:3.19: “Whoever has gone to the Buddha for refuge
dn20:3.20: will not go to the lower worlds.
dn20:3.21: After giving up the human body
dn20:3.22: they will fill up the ranks of the gods.”
dn20:4.1: Then the Fortunate One addressed the monks, saying:
dn20:4.2: “Monks, almost all of the gods from the ten world-elements have assembled to see the Realised One and the Saṅgha of monks.
dn20:4.3: Monks, those who in the past were Worthy Ones, Perfect Sambuddhas, for those Fortunate Ones also at least as many gods have assembled as for me at the present time.
dn20:4.4: Monks, those who in the future will be Worthy Ones, Perfect Sambuddhas, for those Fortunate Ones also at least as many gods will assemble as for me at the present time.
dn20:4.5: Monks, I will declare the names of the hosts of gods,
dn20:4.6: monks, I will proclaim the names of the hosts of gods,
dn20:4.7: monks, I will reveal the names of the hosts of gods.
dn20:4.8: Listen to it, apply your minds well, and I will speak.”
dn20:4.9: “Yes, reverend Sir,” those monks replied to the Fortunate One,
dn20:4.10: and the Fortunate One said this:
